newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TURKISH MINISTER SLAMS `FOREIGN PLAYER' RUSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TURKISH MINISTER SLAMS `FOREIGN PLAYER' RUSE.

text.p: Turkey's sports minister has denounced efforts by top soccer clubs to naturalise foreigners in a bid to evade stringent limits on non-Turkish players.
But Bahattin Seker, state minister responsible for sports, did not say if or how he would act to scupper the clubs' plans.
"I am against giving Turkish citizenship to foreigners who block the progress of local players," Seker told the soccer daily Fanatik on Thursday.
Turkish clubs are allowed to use only three foreign players at any one time.

Turkish champions Fenerbahce have already applied for Nigerian players Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha and Uche Okechukwu to become Turkish nationals, taking the names Muhammed Yavuz Okocha and Abdulkerim Rahim Uche.
Istanbul rivals Besiktas and Galatasaray had been expected to follow suit.
"I don't think it right for a few clubs, in their quest for championship or other gains, to ensure superiority over less greedy clubs by breaching the limit on foreigners," Seker said.
"Breaking the law to use more foreigners is just not nice."
The naturalisations must be approved by the cabinet, the newspaper said.
